newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares mixed, seen stabilising this week.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares mixed, seen stabilising this week.

text.p: Most Polish shares fell in lower turnover on Monday but gains by some heavyweights pushed the main index up and analysts said the market could be entering a consolidation phase.

"The stronger post-price-fixing buying signals a slight gain tomorrow but there could be a slight fall...with the low trade making accidental swings in both directions possible," said Pawel Tarnowski of Raiffeisen Capital and Investment.
Analysts said the market could receive a boost on Tuesday if firms' October earnings reports, most due later on Monday, proved particularly good.
The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.4 percent to 13,619.6 points and turnover fell 11.2 percent to 68.9 million zlotys on both markets. Losers led gainers by 32 to 29 with 19 stocks flat.

Analysts said a positive signal toward the end of the month could be the move to stocks of up to half the capital from the recent 340-million-zloty ($121 million) oversubscription of the initial public offering of Bank Ochrony Srodowiska SA.
They said bank BIG and Bank Gdanski, up 2.4 and two percent respectively, could be helped by BIG's prospective upping its stake in Gdanski now that the government was allowed to sell its 39.9 stake.
BIG currently holds about 30 percent of Gdanski.
Continuous trade turnover was at 1.3 million zlotys ($0.5 million) with the eight stocks seeing action up.
Mass privatisation NFI units were flat at 142 zlotys ($50.5) at the regular bourse session and rose 3.5 percent to 147 zlotys ($52.2) in 22-million-zloty ($7.8 million) continuous trade.
